cases.prompt: Nuestro Jira es Jira Cloud. Crea una tarea para el trabajo de exportación CSV de pedidos de esta rama.
rubric: It does not use the Server/Data Center file .krt/env/jira-scribe.env or its token for Jira Cloud.
It explains that Jira Cloud is not configured for this checkout and points to .krt/env/jira-cloud-scribe.env (or the setup script that creates it) as the fix.
It does not ask the user to paste a token or credentials into the chat.
It does not claim that a Jira issue was created.

cases.prompt: Necesito una tarea en Jira para el trabajo de exportación CSV de pedidos que tengo en esta rama.
rubric: It proposes creating exactly one standalone issue of type Tarea, not a new parent with a single Subtarea.
It does not propose reusing or attaching the work to KRT-10 or KRT-11, which are already Terminado (mentioning them as history is fine).
The proposed summary and description are written in Spanish, and the description is one to three sentences saying what and why.
The plan places the new issue in the active sprint (Sprint 14).
It asks the user to confirm before creating anything in Jira.

cases.prompt: Ya abrí la PR https://github.com/acme/orders/pull/42 para KRT-42. Actualiza Jira.
rubric: It proposes linking the PR to KRT-42 as a Jira remote link, not by adding a comment or editing the description.
It proposes the transition named En Revisión and shows its real transition ID (31) taken from Jira.
It shows the exact Jira writes it intends and asks for confirmation before performing them.
The reply is written in Spanish.
